q-213446.name: Question 1
q-213446.worked_solution:
To remove the radical $\sqrt{7}$ from the denominator, all we need to do is multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{7}$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}} & = \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{7}} & = \\ \frac{1\cdot \sqrt{7}}{(\sqrt{7})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{7}}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{27}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{27}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{27}}{\sqrt{27}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{27}}{(\sqrt{27})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{27}}{27} & \end{aligned}
$$

Next, we notice that $27$ has a perfect square factor $(9).$ Therefore, we can rewrite $\sqrt{27}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{27} & = \\ \sqrt{9\cdot 3} & = \\ \sqrt{9}\cdot \sqrt{3} & = \\ 3\sqrt{3} & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we simplify our original fraction as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{27}}{27} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5}\cdot 3\sqrt{3}}{27} & = \\ \frac{3\cdot \sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{3}}{27} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{3}}{9} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5\cdot 3}}{9} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{15}}{9}\end{aligned}
$$
